evidence: Existing shared instruction/address/stack handlers and normalization; independent bit vector, immediate/captured state and trace comparisons, single-read and CPU/controller integration tests
historical_timing_change: none; the new API uses explicit logical PVR/publication boundaries, not physical K/M signal timings
boundaries: Eleven arithmetic opcodes share one generic instruction handler; no second opcode interpreter.
PVR applies existing address/stack/half advancement; cancellation does not undo already accepted effects.
The same normalizer publishes A/Y before overflow and updates the final arithmetic mode only on success.
Operand read failures retain their cause and are delivered at completion; legacy watchpoint accounting is preserved.
CPU capture and result supply may run inside the owned hardware calendar; dispatch/completion still cannot.
The fault description is latched at operand failure, not rebuilt from a later global LastFault.
Automatic controller binding, read failure microsequence, full timing decode, memory/devices, profiles and OS gate remain incomplete.
